---
title: "F200 Space Exploration worker-speed cap-ten fixture"
---

This disposable fixture prepares one deliberately reduced Factorio 2.0.77 / Space Exploration 0.7.57 / published MIR 5.0.15 worker-speed cap boundary. It is not Gamer433's original save or an ore-mining/productivity reproduction.

The source `0.1.0` role is create-only and requires cap zero. It uses only scripted setup to seed the actual `worker-robots-speed-6` technology at level ten with 27% current work and a repeated queued next occurrence. It explicitly marks the named worker-speed predecessor researched before this setup; the foreign automation queue also has its named automation-science prerequisite. The fixture separately seeds a foreign-disabled level-eleven force with an unrelated 42% queue sentinel and an earned-above-cap level-thirteen force. It creates no lab, consumes no science and receives no actor tick. Its one source marker is an `on_init` scripted-setup snapshot, not a completion or save claim; bounded prerequisite callbacks are labelled administrative rather than ordinary research.

The cap `0.2.0` role sets only `mir-max-level-worker-robots-speed` to ten. After MIR configuration has removed the disallowed queued next occurrence, it records the actual three-force `pre_work` frame before it creates the fixture lab or feeds science. It adds a fixture-only fast lab whose accepted inputs are explicitly the selected technology's actual ingredient names. The fixture never writes the target technology's cost, ingredients or effects. During the pending level-ten work it makes bounded, accepted-count-only input top-ups; it does not presume the full research-unit count fits a lab inventory. One ordinary native completion may occur; the following level-eleven state must be disabled without a second start or debit, while the level-thirteen earned worker-speed bonus remains. A labelled post-completion top-up leaves positive input for every actual ingredient. The lab stays enabled through a two-tick post-completion hold: per-pack input and cumulative scripted-feed values must remain unchanged between the first settled completion observation and the hold end, and a bounded attempt to queue disabled level eleven must leave the queue unchanged. Only then does it save `mir5-worker-speed-cap-ten-complete`; two later cold loads only read, validate and emit one `[MIR_WORKER_SPEED_CAP_TEN phase=cold]` snapshot each.

Each marker serializes its JSON body to `script-output/worker-speed-cap-ten/{source,complete,cold}.json` and logs the same body once. It has the exact active `mods` tuple/count, cap, actual per-level worker-speed effect, full player/foreign/earned force frames, and scripted setup/feed labels. The completion and cold bodies also retain the post-reconcile/pre-feed `pre_work` frame, the one `{name, by_script, tick}` ordinary event, the two-tick hold, disabled-level-eleven queue-attempt result, and lab `input_by_name`/cumulative-feed totals. Thus the source, pre-work and final player queues are independently observable as two occurrences, one retained current occurrence and zero occurrences. The custom lab and its science input are scripted test apparatus, not physical science production evidence. A governed owner must bind the exact package/archive closure and independently review any resulting native output.
